 40s ago 10.23 EST Half time: Charlton 0-4 Chelsea
 Hats off to Charlton for steadying the ship: They were 4-0 down after 13 min.
 View image in fullscreen Anna Koivunen of Charlton Athletic has been busy. Photograph: Darren Woolley/Focus Images Ltd/Shutterstock Share Updated at  10.24 EST 2m ago 10.22 EST Goal (64 min): Brighton 2-1 Palace (Peskett)
 What a turnaround!
 View image in fullscreen Sophie Peskett on the ball. Photograph: Charlie Crowhurst/Getty Images Share Updated at  10.22 EST 3m ago 10.20 EST Goal (59 min): Brighton 2-1 Palace (Hayes)
 All square at Broadfield Stadium.
 Share Updated at  10.21 EST 4m ago 10.20 EST Spurs 3-0 up on Birmingham City, West Ham 3-0 up on Liverpool, Chelsea 4-0 up on Charlton. The only remaining jeopardy, it would seem, is in Brighton v Crystal Palace … and right on cue there’s a goal for Brighton!
 Share 5m ago 10.18 EST Suzanne Wrack One shot , on target and in the back of the net, was all it took for Aston Villa to reopen the wound that Arsenal had been carefully trying to stitch up.
 Despite almost 65% possession, 28 shots to one, and 56 touches in the opposition box to four, Alessia Russo’s 85th-minute goal meant Arsenal were only able to salvage a point against Villa after back-to-back wins in the league and Champions League had appeared to have kickstarted their season.
 Russo spares Arsenal blushes but latest setback increases pressure on Slegers Read more Share 7m ago 10.17 EST Goal (53 min): Birmingham City 0-3 Tottenham (Gaupset)
 Tottenham will be moving up to fourth in the table at this rate.
 Share 12m ago 10.12 EST 40 min: Charlton’s defenders won’t be sorry that James has gone off. It still promises to be a long afternoon – but James was the creative lynchpin for Chelsea during that four-goal salvo.
 If Charlton can make it to half-time at 4-0, they’ve not conceded for over half an hour. That’s actually pretty impressive given how the opening minutes unfolded.
 View image in fullscreen Lauren James has gone off injured after dominating for Chelsea early on. Photograph: Andrew Couldridge/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at  10.16 EST 14m ago 10.10 EST Goal (50 min): Birmingham City 0-2 Spurs (Holdt)
 Olivia Holdt makes it two for Tottenham!
 View image in fullscreen Olivia Holdt. Photograph: Tottenham Hotspur FC/Shutterstock Share 18m ago 10.06 EST 35 min: Half a chance for Jodie Hutton. She gets her head to a cross from the Charlton right. It’s clutching at straws though in truth: Chelsea are completely dominant. Cuthbert is now on the pitch, James having trudged off a while ago and Bompastor’s side briefly playing with 10.
 Share Updated at  10.07 EST 19m ago 10.04 EST 33 min: James has gone down injured. Looks like she may have tweaked a hamstring or a muscle, as it seemed like she just pulled up. Alas, James is going off, but Erin Cuthbert is getting her shinpads on as I write: a very capable replacement.
 Share 22m ago 10.02 EST 30 min : Charlton know the game is gone. But they’ve steadied the ship somewhat in the last 15 minutes. Their defensive shape looks a little better. Can they cause any issues at the other end? It’s been one-way traffic so far.
 View image in fullscreen Lauren James is being brilliant for Chelsea again. Photograph: Andrew Couldridge/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at  10.03 EST 26m ago 09.58 EST This is a baptism of fire for Anna Koivunen on her WSL debut in the Charlton goal. She should have done better with the second goal but aside from that, it’s been fine finishing from Chelsea.
 View image in fullscreen Anna Koivunen of Charlton Athletic (right) reacts as Melvine Malard of Chelsea scores her team’s second goal. Photograph: Alex Davidson/WSL/WSL Football/Getty Images Share Updated at  09.58 EST 28m ago 09.55 EST Half time scores
 Birmingham City 0-1 Spurs
 West Ham 3-0 Liverpool
 Brighton 0-1 Crystal Palace
 Share 30m ago 09.53 EST 22 min: Malard shoots, Malard scores, but it’s offside. No hat-trick but it will surely come. More sensational work from James for Chelsea to make that, who is such a wonderful creative talent.
 Share 33m ago 09.51 EST Goal: 19 min: Charlton 0-4 Chelsea (Malard)
 They were queuing up. This is getting ugly for Charlton. Two for Malard. Karen Hills looks suitably concerned. Her side are being totally outclassed.
 Share Updated at  09.51 EST 35m ago 09.48 EST Goal: 45 min – West Ham 3-0 Liverpool (Codina)
 There’s another WSL game, along with Charlton v Chelsea, that appears to be over.
 Share Updated at  09.50 EST 38m ago 09.45 EST Lauren James cuts in on her right foot, and hammers a shot from the edge, that Koivunen beats out. But it drops to Ellie Carpenter, who applies an excellent finish. True, she had a partly open goal and Koivunen was already on the deck having saved from James, but that’s still a classy finish. This could be a cricket score.
 Share 40m ago 09.44 EST Goal: 13 min: Charlton 0-3 Chelsea (Carpenter)
 Charlton knew it was going to be tough. It is tough.
 View image in fullscreen Ellie Carpenter of Chelsea celebrates with teammate Melvine Malard. Photograph: Alex Davidson/WSL/WSL Football/Getty Images Share Updated at  09.51 EST 41m ago 09.42 EST Goal: 10 min: Charlton 0-2 Chelsea (Malard)
 It’s a scruffy one, after an attack down the Chelsea left, but they all count. The ball hits some part of Melvine Malard’s midriff and bounces into the net. Double trouble for Charlton.
 View image in fullscreen Melvine Malard of Chelsea scores her team’s second goal. Photograph: Alex Davidson/WSL/WSL Football/Getty Images Share Updated at  09.50 EST 43m ago 09.41 EST Goal: 34 min: Brighton 0-1 Palace (Blanchard)
 A goal for Palace in “El Gatwicko”.
 Share 45m ago 09.38 EST Suzanne Wrack Goals from Khadija Shaw and Lauren Hemp helped Manchester City escape from Bromley with three points after a thrilling encounter with London City Lionesses . It was a statement performance from the home team, despite the defeat delivering a blow to any title ambitions they may have been quietly holding on to prior to kick-off.
 The gap between themselves and the champions is now six points, after Hemp restored City’s lead following Jana Fernández’s equaliser. But that London City had even played their way into conversations about this season’s title contenders in their second season has been hugely impressive.
 Manchester City edge out London City Lionesses in thriller after Hemp strikes back Read more Share 46m ago 09.38 EST Goal: 37 min: Birmingham City 0-1 Spurs (Blakstad)
 Julie Blakstad has Tottenham in front.
 Share 48m ago 09.35 EST First, Lauren James is afforded space down the Chelsea left. From the resulting corner, which is taken short, Charlton fail to close down again, and Nathalie Björn climbs highest to nod a fine header back across goal and in.
 Share Updated at  09.36 EST 49m ago 09.34 EST Goal: 3 min: Charlton 0-1 Chelsea (Björn)
 Well, that was easy.
 Share 50m ago 09.33 EST “ We know it’s going to be a tough afternoon,” Karen Hills, the Charlton manager, said before kick-off. “We relish the opportunity. It’s going to be tough today. There is no hiding behind the fact. We will try to make it as uncomfortable as possible for Chelsea.”
 Share 52m ago 09.32 EST First half kick-off
 Charlton v Chelsea is go.
 Share 53m ago 09.30 EST “ We respect every team in this league ,” Bompastor tells the BBC.
 “Every game is three points. Today is no different. We have to come here with the desire to put in a good performance, and bring the three points home.
 “It’s important to rotate for a club like us. It’s a balance between opportunities for players who are performing at a good level, and training well … and maintaining a good level of performance.”
 Share 1h ago 09.27 EST Charlton v Chelsea teams
 Sonia Bompastor makes seven changes to the Chelsea team. Three for Charlton: Karen Hills hands a WSL debut to Anna Koivunen in goal.
 Charlton Women: Koivunen, Johnston, Skeels, Lobato, Mason, Neville, Van Egmond, Flannery, Hutton, Korhonen, Davidson. Substitutes : Whitehouse, Humphrey, Azzaro, Kenney, Fitzgerald, Lockwood, Waldie, Robe, Nelson-Iye.
 Chelsea Women: Hampton, Bjorn, McCabe, Buurman, Carpenter, Walsh, Nusken, Baltimore, Matsukubo, James, Malard. Substitutes : Peng, Cuthbert, Thompson, Dragoni, Kaptein, Bronze, Hamano, Buchanan, Beever-Jones.
 Share Updated at  09.31 EST 1h ago 09.23 EST Goal: West Ham 2-0 Liverpool (Wandeler)
 Leila Wandeler doubles West Ham’s money.
 View image in fullscreen And another! Photograph: Keeran Marquis/KDMP/SPP/Shutterstock Share Updated at  09.26 EST 1h ago 09.21 EST Charlton are rock-bottom of the WSL, with zero points to show from seven matches.
 Chelsea are second, with six wins out of seven, and can pull level with City with a win.
 Share Updated at  09.22 EST 1h ago 09.19 EST Worth revisiting some Arsenal v Villa stats quickly.
 Corners: Arsenal 10, Villa 0
 Passes attempted: Arsenal 584, Villa 338
 Shots on goal: Arsenal 8, Villa 1
 Shots: Arsenal 28, Villa 1
 xG: Arsenal 2.61, Villa 0.07.
 Final score: Arsenal 1-1 Aston Villa
 Share Updated at  09.19 EST 1h ago 09.15 EST “ I Was Monty’s Double ” is just finishing on BBC2. And we all know what means.
 View image in fullscreen Charlton v Chelsea is about to start! (Thinks John Mills.) Photograph: Moviestore/REX/Shutterstock Share Updated at  09.20 EST 1h ago 09.10 EST Goal: 7 min: West Ham 1-0 Liverpool (Asseyi pen)
 Asseyi, to whom Suzanne Wrack spoke this week, has already hit the onion bag for the Hammers with a seventh-minute penalty.
 View image in fullscreen Viviane Asseyi of West Ham United celebrates with teammates. Photograph: Elli Birch/WSL/WSL Football/Getty Images West Ham’s Viviane Asseyi: ‘When I was four I said I wanted to be like Zidane’ Read more Share Updated at  09.14 EST 1h ago 09.09 EST West Ham v Liverpool and Brighton v Palace both kicked off at 2pm. The action is non-stop today. Charlton v Chelsea is the game we’ll be focusing on, and that’s a 2.30pm GMT kick-off.
 Share 1h ago 09.05 EST West Ham v Liverpool teams
 West Ham: Picaud, Riesen, Codina, Cascarino, Belloumou, Piubel, Zelem, Siren, Asseyi, Wandeler, Gago. Substitutes : Walsh, Endo, Kumagai, Ueki, Nystrom, Tinnebo, Salmon, Morgan, Peacock.
 Liverpool: Keating, Kerr, Clark, Fisk, Bernabe, Nagano, Bergstrom, Kapocs, Ramos, MacLean, Olsson. Substitutes : Kirby, Parry, Endemann, Enderby, Hobinger, Agrez, Itamura, Ward, Trueman.
 Share Updated at  09.06 EST 1h ago 09.03 EST Brighton v Palace teams
 Brighton & Hove Albion Women: Nnadozie, Mpome, Hayes, Vanegas, Olislagers, Peskett, Symonds, Joramo, Garcia, Kirby, Tvedten. Substitutes : Loeck, Heeps, George, Rayner, Auee, Murphy, Warren, Gay.
 Crystal Palace Women: Peyraud-Magnin, Bartrip, Everett, Goldie, Napier, Hopcroft, Ladd, O’Brien, Blanchard, Larkin, England. Substitutes : Yanez, Enge, Lloyd-Smith, Sharpe, Howat, Weerden, Cosme, Nolan, Swaby.
 Share 1h ago 09.01 EST “ Best WSL game I’ve seen for a long time,” writes Gordon in Abderdeen, of London City Lionesses v Manchester City.
 “A steal by City; but winning football matches means composed finishing and LCL didn’t have that. Tremendous resilience shown by City earned them the win.”
